title: About
text:
I completed an M.A. in Geography Education and an integrated major in Applied Data Science at Seoul National University in 2026. My master’s research examined whether large language model representations could reproduce spatial interaction in Seoul mobility flows.
I approach machine learning as a tool for geographic questions. I am most interested in models that account for spatial context, uneven performance across places, and bias in mobility data.

title: Woohyung Kim
text:
Human mobility and spatial data science




I develop methods for spatial analysis and study how people move between places.


I use machine learning to measure how places resemble one another and to model the flows that connect them. I examine where mobility predictions fail and whose travel the underlying data capture.

title: Woohyung Kim
text:
Selected work



Journal article · Geographical Analysis · 2026


ML-SAS: A Machine-Learning-Based Spatial Autocorrelation Statistic for Mixed-Type Data
I used machine learning to measure similarity between regions described by different types of attributes, then used those similarities to measure global and local spatial autocorrelation.
Woohyung Kim and Sang-Il Lee. Geographical Analysis, 58(4), e70062.
Paper (DOI) · R package · Reproduction code




Submitted manuscript · The Professional Geographer


Evaluating frozen language-model representations for urban mobility prediction
Using hourly flows between Seoul’s 25 districts, I tested whether language-model representations of place and time improve a gravity model. They reduced average prediction error, but the combined model still overpredicted travel on several high-volume connections.
